meta.purpose: SPDX license IDs whose assets MAY be re-hosted / republished in the blog. The validate.py media gate hard-fails any sourced asset whose license.spdx is not in `allow`, or whose permits_republication != true.

notes: Unsplash-License / Pexels-License / Pixabay-License are free-for-commercial-use, no-attribution-required stock licenses whose terms permit downloading, modifying, and embedding the photo on a public web page — so they are genuinely re-hostable here, unlike NC/ND Creative Commons variants. They are NOT SPDX identifiers (no canonical SPDX id exists); we use these stable names as the allowlist key, and fetch_stock.py / fetch_openverse.py mirror the same three so they self-flag permits_republication consistently. Attribution is appreciated but not required (set requires_attribution=false); still record the photographer + source in attribution_text as a courtesy + provenance. They forbid (a) selling the unaltered photo as stock and (b) using identifiable people/brands in a way that implies endorsement — neither applies to an illustrative blog backdrop, but keep real-person identity verification on (identity.verified=true) regardless.
NC (non-commercial) and ND (no-derivatives) are NOT allowed — a published demo is effectively commercial and re-laid-out (derivative).
Copyrighted commercial music / video must NOT be re-hosted; use a kind=embed instance instead (the official platform player carries its own license).

Royalty-free-with-terms tracks (e.g. a production-music library, Pixabay Music): set spdx to the library's identifier and permits_republication=true ONLY if the licence text clearly allows web embedding (with attribution where required).
'Fair use' is NOT a re-host license here — it is too risky for a public viral demo. Downgrade to an embed or drop.
